_comment: Recorded cost ratios (anchorHz / benchHz) for the performance gate. Update deliberately, in the same PR as an intentional perf change, and say why in the PR description. Costs are dimensionless: they express 'this benchmark costs N noise-anchor operations', so they stay comparable across machines and CI runner classes.
recordedFrom: Original cohort: https://github.com/melpomenex/Incrementum/actions/runs/31182419989. Tab-workspace additions and SM-20 runner-class correction: median of three calibrated Linux x86_64 / Node 22.22.1 runs on 2026-08-13. Anki import Node 24 correction: median of runs 31736712215 and attempts 1-2 of 31737723373. PDF-reflow hot paths (point/rect round trips, canonical anchor resolution): first add-pdf-reflow implementation session, local bench:check run.

sm20/review-sequence.reason: reviewM2/reviewM3 replaced structuredClone of the optimizer/matrices (recursive walk of ~57k elements + nested cubes) with hand-written shallow copies (.slice of each mutable array, per-row/per-cell for the number[][][] cubes). ~26x faster, byte-identical output; the commit:false clone is the per-review hot path. Re-recorded as the median of three calibrated runs (13.00, 13.87, 14.46) because this long allocation-heavy path scales differently from the gate's median mixed-workload runner calibration; the longer 2s/100-iteration sample supports tightening tolerance from 1.6x to the 1.25x default.

queue/build-500-items.reason: queueScrollBudget.splitReviewBudget (two Math.mins) was replaced by composeSession: three-way weight normalization, documents-anchored session sizing, iterated proportional redistribution of unfillable shares, and largest-remainder apportionment. ~11x the (near-free) baseline cost, still ~0.05us per composition; runs once per session build.

queueScrollOrder/combined-sort-300-items.reason: SuperMemo combined-criterion session sort: hoisted the per-item-invariant score terms (priority + jitterWeight*stableJitter(id), and the topic/item classification) out of the O(n^2) selection loop into precomputed Float64/Uint8 arrays, and lifted the two type-specific proportion terms to once-per-position. stableJitter (a BigInt FNV-1a hash) was the dominant cost, recomputed ~n^2 times for n distinct values. ~38x faster; output byte-identical (verified by differential fuzzing, 17732 checks, 0 mismatches).

neuralQueue/spreading-activation-300-nod.reason: SuperMemo neural-queue spreading-activation pass (Phase 4): TS port of the Rust algorithm, propagating activation over a 300-node seeded tree via concept/inter-element/descendant/sibling links with the monotonicity InsertOrUpdate. Runs only on neural-queue depletion (< 20 remaining); the ~0.9us cost reflects the pure-combine hot path. Wider tolerance because Map operations are GC-sensitive at this timescale.

ankiImport/convert-2000-notes.reason: convertAnkiCardsToLearningItems did deck.notes.find(n => n.id === card.noteId) inside the card loop, an O(n) linear scan of all notes per card (O(n^2) overall, ~4M comparisons for 2000 cards). Indexed notes by id in a first-wins Map once before the loop (preserving Array.find's first-match semantics), so each lookup is O(1). Byte-identical for all finite-integer ids (verified by differential testing); NaN ids would differ but are unreachable (Rust producer types ids as i64 from SQLite). Re-recorded as the median of three unchanged-code Linux x86_64 / Node 24.18.0 CI samples (1.202, 1.408, 1.368) after GitHub Actions moved the LTS runner from Node 22 to Node 24; the 1.25x tolerance remains unchanged.

tabs/normalize-pane-tree-depth-4.reason: Sub-microsecond tree normalization is timer- and GC-sensitive, so it uses the same wider tolerance as other microbenchmarks.

tabs-dom/mount-12-tab-workspace.reason: jsdom mount cost includes React scheduling and garbage collection variance.

tabs-dom/switch-active-tab-12-tabs.reason: jsdom interaction cost includes React scheduling and garbage collection variance.

tabs-dom/rerender-on-tab-collection-chan.reason: jsdom rerender cost includes React scheduling and garbage collection variance.
